final_answer:
Two high-criticality FMEA risks fit: **FM-02** and **FM-13**. Each has passed OQ test coverage, no PQ test case traces to it, and its own current controls say PQ is expected.

**How I checked.** I took the 10 HIGH-class items in the process FMEA (RA-PFMEA-001). I followed each from risk to the URS requirement it mitigates, then to the test cases that verify that requirement. I also followed requirements down through any FS/CS specs to their test cases. I then sorted the test cases by protocol type (OQ or PQ).

**Findings**
- **FM-02** (wrong or edited selection program, Prodigy):
  - It maps to URS-PRDG-002, the locked, version-controlled program requirement.
  - That requirement is verified only by TC-OQ-PRDG-02 (OQ-PRDG-01).
  - The only Prodigy PQ test case, TC-PQ-PRDG-01, covers closed-system processing (URS-PRDG-001) and not program control.
  - The FMEA's own control is "Locked programs, Prodigy OQ/PQ".
- **FM-13** (deviation from the programmed freeze curve, controlled-rate freezer):
  - It maps to URS-CRF-001, verified only by TC-OQ-CRF-01 (OQ-CRF-01, empty-chamber run of profile CRF-P01).
  - There is no CRF PQ protocol or test case in the database, only IQ and OQ.
  - The FMEA control is "CRF OQ; PQ by engineering runs", so PQ evidence is expected but absent.

**Excluded**
- **FM-03, FM-07, FM-09** are mitigated by a requirement that has both OQ and PQ (Prodigy closed system, ULT -70 °C hold, incubator temperature mapping). FM-07's high-temperature alarm requirement is OQ-only, but its chamber-temperature requirement has PQ.
- **FM-05, FM-06, FM-14, FM-15** depend on EBR or LIMS functions, which have OQ functional testing only. No PQ protocol exists for those systems and none is expected.
- **FM-16** (incubator door left open) has OQ coverage only, through the OQ door-alarm test TC-OQ-INC-04, which had one FAIL among its executions. Its controls cite alarms, escalation and training rather than PQ, so I treated it as borderline and did not include it. Include it if you consider incubator PQ expected for every incubator risk.

Two high-criticality FMEA risks fit: **FM-02** and **FM-13**. Each has passed OQ test coverage, no PQ test case traces to it, and its own current controls say PQ is expected.

**How I checked.** I took the 10 HIGH-class items in the process FMEA (RA-PFMEA-001). I followed each from risk to the URS requirement it mitigates, then to the test cases that verify that requirement. I also followed requirements down through any FS/CS specs to their test cases. I then sorted the test cases by protocol type (OQ or PQ).

**Findings**
- **FM-02** (wrong or edited selection program, Prodigy):
  - It maps to URS-PRDG-002, the locked, version-controlled program requirement.
  - That requirement is verified only by TC-OQ-PRDG-02 (OQ-PRDG-01).
  - The only Prodigy PQ test case, TC-PQ-PRDG-01, covers closed-system processing (URS-PRDG-001) and not program control.
  - The FMEA's own control is "Locked programs, Prodigy OQ/PQ".
- **FM-13** (deviation from the programmed freeze curve, controlled-rate freezer):
  - It maps to URS-CRF-001, verified only by TC-OQ-CRF-01 (OQ-CRF-01, empty-chamber run of profile CRF-P01).
  - There is no CRF PQ protocol or test case in the database, only IQ and OQ.
  - The FMEA control is "CRF OQ; PQ by engineering runs", so PQ evidence is expected but absent.

**Excluded**
- **FM-03, FM-07, FM-09** are mitigated by a requirement that has both OQ and PQ (Prodigy closed system, ULT -70 °C hold, incubator temperature mapping). FM-07's high-temperature alarm requirement is OQ-only, but its chamber-temperature requirement has PQ.
- **FM-05, FM-06, FM-14, FM-15** depend on EBR or LIMS functions, which have OQ functional testing only. No PQ protocol exists for those systems and none is expected.
- **FM-16** (incubator door left open) has OQ coverage only, through the OQ door-alarm test TC-OQ-INC-04, which had one FAIL among its executions. Its controls cite alarms, escalation and training rather than PQ, so I treated it as borderline and did not include it. Include it if you consider incubator PQ expected for every incubator risk.
